conviction_note: Two measurements. Each finding is sized on its own, and they sum to +1.55. The largest is guidance arithmetic from the company's own releases: the FY ex-promote guide implies $1.55-1.59 a quarter for H2, below Q2's $1.60 run-rate, even though occupancy is rising and the mark-to-market is 17%. That points to a beat and a third raise. The rest are small public proxies and the August equity raise. The scaled number is abs_move 3.8 (the option-implied 3.5, nudged up because a guide change is likely) times a p_up of 62 (a lean on a primary-document number plus 7 of 7 up reactions, held below 65 because the beat-and-raise habit is widely known and the 5-day run-up of +4.3% has pre-bought some of it), giving +0.91. The scaled number is smaller than the sum because the sign uncertainty sits in p_up.
bar: Q3 2026 Core FFO consensus $1.57-1.58. Sources: Benzinga forecasts (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLD/earnings-forecasts) and EarningsWhispers ($1.57, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/PLD), both via search snippets. The company guide gives the same number: FY Core FFO $6.22-6.30 (Q2 release, https://ir.prologis.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1044/prologis-reports-second-quarter-2026-results) less H1 $3.13 ($1.50 Q1 + $1.63 Q2) leaves $3.09-3.17 for H2, about $1.565 a quarter. The bar is sourced, so sizes are not capped. I expect about $1.60-1.61, roughly +2% versus the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 18.47M shares on the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 1.98% of 932M shares outstanding, 4.91 days to cover. It was 13.45M on 2026-07-15, so it rose about 5M after the SEGRO share offer, consistent with merger-arb hedges rather than a fundamental short (https://equibles.com/stocks/pld/shortinterest, read 2026-10-14). Not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is +1.69 vol points, a mild put bid, and put/call open interest is 0.52, call-heavy. The baseline reads the priced lean as 'balanced'. Spot $132.72 is 11.6% below the 52-week high and below the August offering price of $139.85.

findings.finding: On the company's own numbers the guide looks conservative. H1 2026 Core FFO ex-promote was $3.12 ($1.52 Q1 + $1.60 Q2), and the FY ex-promote guide of $6.22-6.30 implies $1.55-1.59 a quarter for H2, below Q2's $1.60. Meanwhile period-end occupancy (95.5%) is above the Q2 average (95.0%), cash same-store NOI ran 8.5%, and the 17% lease mark-to-market keeps rolling in. That sets up a Q3 beat of about $0.02-0.04 and a third FY raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prologis raised FY Core FFO at Q1 2026 ($6.00-6.20 to $6.07-6.23) and at Q2 2026 (to $6.22-6.30). The stock rose on all 7 prints in the baseline: +1.72% on 2026-04-16, +4.63% on 2026-07-16, +6.33% on Q3 2025 (2025-10-15). Mean about +3.3%, median 1.84%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.57-1.58 sits on the guide-implied H2 run-rate, not on Q2's $1.60 ex-promote. If the street had priced a Q3 at or above the Q2 run-rate, consensus would be $1.60 or higher. The stock is 11.6% below its high and below the $139.85 August offering price, which is not what a pre-priced third raise looks like. Partly priced: the 5-day run-up is +4.3% and the beat-and-raise habit is well known.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (Core FFO $1.50, ex-promote $1.52; https://ir.prologis.com/press-releases/detail/1036/prologis-reports-first-quarter-2026-results) is a separate document, but it is the same company and the same arithmetic. CFO Arndt on 2026-09-15 expected 2027 same-store NOI growth 'about the same' as 2026 and called mid-single-digit market rent growth 'conservative' (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/pld/transcripts/750835-bofa-ny-global-real-estate-conference-2026/).

findings.finding: At the BofA conference on 2026-09-15, CFO Tim Arndt said Q3 lease signings should land 'in that ZIP code' of the recent records (about 60-65M sf; Q2 was over 67M sf), that 'the first few months have been great', and that the pipeline is 'well over 100 million square feet' of inquiries.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record leasing headlined Q2 2026 (67M sf), and the stock rose +4.63% that day. Leasing volume is reported alongside the guide, so it cannot be isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It was said in public a month ago and is within what management pre-signalled. The only part that could surprise is a Q3 at or above the 67M sf record versus the 60-65M sf the CFO framed. If that were in the price, the stock would not be trading below the August offering price.
findings.independence: Cushman & Wakefield's Q3 national data (next finding) points the same way, but it is a different document.

findings.finding: Cushman & Wakefield's Q3 2026 national industrial report shows net absorption of 76.6M sf, the strongest quarter since Q1 2023 and the second in a row above 70M. National vacancy fell to 6.8%, and data-center and AI infrastructure was more than 8% of new leasing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific reaction history on industry absorption. The Q3 2025 print, which Prologis called an 'inflection', rose +6.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was published 2026-10-09 and probably accounts for part of the +4.3% 5-day run-up. It is a broad proxy that the company has not confirmed for itself. If it were fully priced, PLD would have recovered to the $139-144 pre-offering range.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not a company number. IREI carries the same Cushman figures (https://irei.com/news/u-s-industrial-demand-accelerates-as-vacancy-falls-2/), so that is one source, not two.

findings.finding: Southern California is Prologis's largest market and stayed soft in Q3 2026. CBRE's Inland Empire report has asking rents flat at $1.08 NNN, taking rates down 3.8%, and new leasing down 28% quarter on quarter. Savills has IE vacancy at 9.9%, up 20bp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SoCal rent declines were the main drag in 2025, through the Q3 2025 print, and the stock still rose on every print.
findings.why_not_priced: Regional broker data that few sell-side previews use. It is narrow, though. The national series is positive, and the company itself said on 2026-09-15 that it is over 96% occupied in SoCal, so the transmission to Prologis's own numbers is weak. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Savills Inland Empire Q3 2026 (https://www.savills.us/research_articles/256536/395121-0) agrees on softness. The CFO's SoCal occupancy comment (BofA transcript) cuts against the transmission to Prologis.

findings.finding: Prologis sold 17.25M new shares at $139.85 on 2026-08-04/07: 15M base plus the 2.25M over-allotment, net about $2.4bn. That is about 1.85% more shares, issued after the July guide was set, and the proceeds pre-fund a SEGRO deal that closes in H1 2027. That is a small per-share FFO carry drag that the July guide did not include.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with a pre-funded equity raise in the baseline window. The stock went from $144.15 on Aug 3 to about $130 on Sep 30, so the issue and the deal have already been absorbed in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: The share count is public. What is not public is how the Q3 guide treats the carry (about 17M shares times $6.26 is about $108M a year of FFO claim, against roughly $90-96M of interest on $2.4bn), which could make any raise smaller than in past quarters. What does the money buy: the SEGRO combination, approved by SEGRO shareholders on 2026-09-28. That is a visible use, so the sign is near zero and slightly negative only on near-term per-share math.

findings.finding: SEGRO shareholders approved the Prologis scheme at the Court and General Meetings on 2026-09-28. The Q3 call is the first earnings forum since then where management can quantify accretion and integration for the combined platform, which has 100% market overlap in the UK/Europe.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came during a pending acquisition of this size. The stock fell from $144 to about $130 between the August deal announcement and the end of September.
findings.why_not_priced: The vote itself is priced. What is not priced is any 2027 accretion number on the call. If the market already credited accretion, the stock would not sit below the $139.85 offering price.
findings.independence: The scheme timetable (court meeting set for 2026-09-28) is at https://hedgeco.net/news/?p=95707. Same event.

outside_window.finding: SEGRO scheme court sanction and regulatory clearances, with completion targeted for H1 2027 (long-stop 2027-08-04). Flowback of the new PLD shares to UK holders comes after that.
The first 2027 guide is due with Q4 results in January 2027. The CFO has signalled 2027 same-store NOI growth 'about the same' as 2026.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 8-Ks after 2026-08-06: none. The Form 4s of 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-02 are routine director deferred-stock conversions and fee deferrals (e.g. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045609/000119312526396712/ownership.xml), with no open-market insider selling.
Prologis data-center announcements in Aug-Oct 2026: nothing found after the July San Jose 99MW filing.
Analyst rating changes in October 2026: none found.
Industrial REIT peers reporting or pre-announcing before 2026-10-15: none found.
Prologis IBI / Prologis Research Q3 2026 publication: not found.

rejected_candidates.detail: The Q2 2026 release gives development starts of $4.5-5.5B, and contributions and dispositions as separate raised lines.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A Q3 '26 FY GAAP EPS consensus of $3.36 used as a bar.
rejected_candidates.detail: The company's FY net earnings guide is $4.40-4.55 (Q2 release). The figure is not a usable bar.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive, in line with the 7-of-7 up reaction history and the call-heavy open interest. They run mildly against the +1.69 put skew, which is small, and partly with the +4.3% 5-day run-up, which has already bought some of the industry-absorption news.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside what was guided): the CFO's Q3 leasing framing is what management already told the market, so that finding went from +0.5 to +0.2.

Rule 5 (narrow proxy vs broad series and a company statement): the Inland Empire softness finding went from -0.3 to -0.1, because the national series is positive and the company says it is over 96% occupied in SoCal. The national Cushman proxy went from +0.4 to +0.3 as unconfirmed transmission.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the equity raise funds a visible, shareholder-approved acquisition, so the finding went from -0.3 to -0.15.
Rules 1 and 6 left the guidance finding at +1.2. The bar is sourced to the company guide and two estimate sources, and this name has paid for raises on 7 of 7 prints.
Rule 8 and the core's understatement note moved abs_move_pct from 3.5 to 3.8. p_up stays at 62.
